title: Admit the best. Are the traits linked?
hook: Talent and looks are unrelated in the crowd. What about among the few who get picked?

knows: correlation means two things rise and fall together (confounding)
doesNotKnow: that selecting on a sum creates a link between independent traits

misconception: If two traits are unrelated in the population they are unrelated in any group.
objective: The learner can say that admitting people whose talent plus looks is high makes the two traits negatively related among those admitted, though they are independent in the whole crowd.
keyState: Cut at 0 (49% admitted, r = -0.44) and at 1.5 (14% admitted, r = -0.63), after seeing r = +0.01 for everyone.

claims.text: In the crowd, talent and looks are generated as independent standard normal numbers (1,500 people).
claims.source: model.ts make(): Box-Muller from mulberry32(31); the stage shows r = +0.01 for everyone (computed from the dots).

claims.text: Admitting people whose talent plus looks is above 1.5 admits about 14% of them.
Among the admitted (sum above 0, 49% of the crowd) the correlation is -0.44; among the top 14% it is -0.63.
claims.source: Computed from the stage's dots with seed 31 (untuned, first seed tried). Over 300 other seeds of 1,500 people: r at cut 0 averaged -0.47 (range -0.57 to -0.37); at cut 1.5 it averaged -0.68 (range -0.78 to -0.51); for 200,000 people -0.46 and -0.67. So the sign is robust, the size varies.

claims.text: Selecting on the sum makes the traits negatively related inside the admitted group even though they are independent overall.
claims.source: Berkson's paradox: conditioning on talent + looks above a cut means a lower value of one trait must be offset by a higher value of the other. Berkson, J. (1946), Biometrics Bulletin 2(3): 47-53, described it in hospital data. The lesson is about the model only.

claims.text: Correlation r runs from -1 to +1: 0 means no linear relationship and negative means one trait is higher when the other is lower.
claims.source: Definition of Pearson's correlation; the stage readout is computed by corr() in model.ts.

recall.question: A college admits only students with a high sum of sports and maths scores. Among its students, what would you expect to see between sports and maths scores?
options: A negative link, even if they are unrelated in all teenagers
recall.why: Admission selects on the sum, so a student weak in one skill must be strong in the other: a negative link appears among those admitted.
